5:### lesson:cartographer-subagent-wrong-checkout-root
8:- statement: A Cartographer subagent dispatched at the reconcile step, given the worktree's absolute path in its dispatch prompt, wrote all its architecture-doc edits (docs/architecture/packets/*.md, index.md, overlays/*.yml, a new decisions/*.md file) to the MAIN CHECKOUT instead of the assigned worktree -- a git-invisible failure caught only because the dispatching commander independently ran git status in BOTH locations. Recovery: capture each file's diff/content before touching anything, revert the main checkout to clean, re-apply the identical changes to the worktree, THEN VERIFY THE REAPPLIED CONTENT IS ACTUALLY COMMITTED ON THE BRANCH (not just present on the worktree filesystem) -- a second, distinct failure mode chained onto the same incident: cmdr-663's own 'reapplied + verified' self-report was inaccurate because the reapply was never committed, and check_arch_map stays green with or without the map node so it can't catch the gap. Re-verify both ends plus the worktree's own architecture-map checker AND confirm the branch diff includes the map files before trusting the recovery.
20:### lesson:consumed-frozen-module-run-guard-tests
23:- statement: When a gate's plan ADDS to a previously-ratified/frozen/consumed module, its acceptance criteria MUST explicitly include re-running that module's OWN pre-existing test file(s), not just the newly authored tests for the new content. Verifying only your own new tests can pass while silently breaking the guard tests of the module you are extending.
35:### lesson:mandatory-full-chain-smoke-before-unattended-run
38:- statement: For an unattended/AFK run that builds a multi-stage pipeline, gate the build on a MANDATORY end-to-end smoke on one real slice BEFORE the unattended run (not just unit tests) -- integration-only silent-correctness bugs (e.g. a provenance/branch inversion) pass every unit test and surface only when the whole chain runs against real data.
50:### lesson:season-batch-runner-per-round-fault-isolation
53:- statement: A real-data multi-round/multi-item batch runner over the epic-659 pipeline MUST isolate per-item failures (try/except-per-item -> PARK with a diagnosis + continue), never let one item's exception kill the whole batch. The pipeline is strictly-pre: E's car ceiling needs sessions with round_idx < R, so early rounds with no strictly-prior data (round 1, sometimes 2) legitimately produce no severity classes and crash inside run_circuit -- expect them to PARK, and smoke an EARLY/edge round (expected to park), not just a mid-season happy path, before launching a long detached batch. Synthetic-runner unit tests do NOT exercise this real-data early-round property.
65:### lesson:verify-subagent-self-report-not-just-green-check
68:- statement: A subagent's (crew, cartographer, or Commander's) own claim of having done/verified/reapplied something is not reliable ground truth on its own, and a green mechanical check (e.g. check_arch_map) can be structurally blind to content drift by construction. When a cheap independent re-derivation is available -- re-run the check yourself on the pinned interpreter, grep/diff the actual artifact, reverse-scan real source against a claimed map -- do it before trusting the claim, especially for architecture-map/content-correctness claims.
80:### lesson:constellation-slash-workid-parsing-gaps
83:- statement: Multiple constellation-commander scripts assume a work_id has no internal '/', breaking under this repo's own nested Commander-under-Admiral convention (epic-<N>/<issue>, e.g. epic-659/665). CONFIRMED TWICE, independently, in the SAME run: (1) run_crew.py --verify-result <session>: load_registry_for_resume parses work_id as session.split('/')[1] (one segment), dropping everything after the first '/'. (2) verify_agent_feedback.py --phase archive: _current_run_archive_dirs string-matches path.name == work_id or path.name.endswith(f'-{work_id}') -- both unsatisfiable when work_id contains '/'. Workarounds used: (1) call run_crew's registry functions directly, bypassing the CLI parser; (2) a FORCED self-waive on archive.c1 with --force + authority=commander-self, citing this exact defect.

1	"""Own-DB SQLite persistence for the DriverFingerprint cell store (issue #666, g2).
2	
3	Mirrors the house store pattern (``src/physics/utilization/reference_utilization_store.py``,
4	``src/physics/layer2/grip_store.py``): ``sqlite3.Row`` factory, create-on-construct unless
5	``must_exist``, ``INSERT OR REPLACE`` idempotency, and an additive ``_migrate_missing_columns``
6	self-heal. This is an OWN database (#632) -- NEVER an ``f1_data*.db``, NEVER the #664
7	``driver_class_observables`` db.
8	
9	This store is a keystone state store: every downstream fingerprint consumer trusts its
10	invariants (Protected Intent). It structurally enforces four things:
11	
12	* **Non-NULL cell_key** -- the primary key is ``CellAddress.cell_key`` (already validated
13	  non-empty in ``address.py``); the column is ALSO declared ``NOT NULL`` here
14	  (belt-and-suspenders with the value-object validation, per the handoff).
15	* **k-cells-always-populated** -- ``write_fingerprint`` always writes exactly ``k`` rows
16	  (one per ``vocabulary.class_ids``); a class with no or thin support gets a
17	  ``status="unresolved"`` row (``NULL`` mean/sigma), never a missing row.
18	  ``get_fingerprint`` always returns exactly ``k`` cells for the same reason -- a class with
19	  no stored row is synthesized as an ``"unresolved"`` cell, not omitted.
20	* **Loud refusal, no silent substitution** -- (1) ``era`` must equal ``vocabulary.rules_era``
21	  on both read and write (the two are separate arguments that both assert an era; if they
22	  disagree there is no principled way to silently pick one, so this refuses); (2) writing
23	  a (driver, era, channel, what_measure) that already carries stored cells under a
24	  DIFFERENT ``vocabulary_version`` refuses (vocabulary drift -- a stale prior taxonomy's
25	  rows would otherwise silently coexist with a new taxonomy's rows under the same logical
26	  slot); (3) writing a non-``"PASS"`` ``ClassVocabulary`` refuses (via
27	  ``ClassVocabulary.require_fittable()``, unless ``allow_unverified=True``); (4) writing a
28	  ``RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES`` slot refuses (Build-2 dormant slot, not populated in Build 1).
29	* **NO fit-on-read** -- this module imports nothing from a fit/pooling/observables module,
30	  and ``get_fingerprint`` never computes a value: a miss synthesizes an ``"unresolved"``
31	  placeholder from ``vocabulary.class_ids`` alone (no observation, no computation), it never
32	  triggers a fit.
33	"""
34	from __future__ import annotations
35	
36	import sqlite3
37	from dataclasses import dataclass
38	from pathlib import Path
39	from typing import Mapping, Optional
40	
41	from src.physics.fingerprint.address import RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES, CellAddress
42	from src.physics.fingerprint.frozen_constants import FINGERPRINT_FROZEN
43	from src.physics.fingerprint.vocabulary import ClassVocabulary
44	
45	# Store-format version, recorded on every row so a future schema evolution can branch on it.
46	FORMAT_VERSION: str = "1"
47	
48	# Default OWN database path (data artifact, NOT committed, NEVER an f1_data DB). Tests pass
49	# an explicit temp path (#656).
50	DEFAULT_DB_PATH: str = "data/driver_fingerprint.db"
51	
52	_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR: float = float(FINGERPRINT_FROZEN["FINGERPRINT_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR"])
53	
54	_RESOLVED = "resolved"
55	_UNRESOLVED = "unresolved"
56	
57	_COLUMNS = (
58	    "cell_key", "driver", "era", "vocabulary_version", "class_id", "channel",
59	    "what_measure", "mean", "sigma", "support_n", "status",
60	    "shared_floor_applied", "format_version",
61	)
62	
63	
64	class EraVocabularyMismatchError(RuntimeError):
65	    """Raised on any era/vocabulary identity inconsistency -- no silent substitution.
66

"""Own-DB SQLite persistence for the DriverFingerprint cell store (issue #666, g2).

Mirrors the house store pattern (``src/physics/utilization/reference_utilization_store.py``,
``src/physics/layer2/grip_store.py``): ``sqlite3.Row`` factory, create-on-construct unless
``must_exist``, ``INSERT OR REPLACE`` idempotency, and an additive ``_migrate_missing_columns``
self-heal. This is an OWN database (#632) -- NEVER an ``f1_data*.db``, NEVER the #664
``driver_class_observables`` db.

This store is a keystone state store: every downstream fingerprint consumer trusts its
invariants (Protected Intent). It structurally enforces four things:

* **Non-NULL cell_key** -- the primary key is ``CellAddress.cell_key`` (already validated
  non-empty in ``address.py``); the column is ALSO declared ``NOT NULL`` here
  (belt-and-suspenders with the value-object validation, per the handoff).
* **k-cells-always-populated** -- ``write_fingerprint`` always writes exactly ``k`` rows
  (one per ``vocabulary.class_ids``); a class with no or thin support gets a
  ``status="unresolved"`` row (``NULL`` mean/sigma), never a missing row.
  ``get_fingerprint`` always returns exactly ``k`` cells for the same reason -- a class with
  no stored row is synthesized as an ``"unresolved"`` cell, not omitted.
* **Loud refusal, no silent substitution** -- (1) ``era`` must equal ``vocabulary.rules_era``
  on both read and write (the two are separate arguments that both assert an era; if they
  disagree there is no principled way to silently pick one, so this refuses); (2) writing
  a (driver, era, channel, what_measure) that already carries stored cells under a
  DIFFERENT ``vocabulary_version`` refuses (vocabulary drift -- a stale prior taxonomy's
  rows would otherwise silently coexist with a new taxonomy's rows under the same logical
  slot); (3) writing a non-``"PASS"`` ``ClassVocabulary`` refuses (via
  ``ClassVocabulary.require_fittable()``, unless ``allow_unverified=True``); (4) writing a
  ``RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES`` slot refuses (Build-2 dormant slot, not populated in Build 1).
* **NO fit-on-read** -- this module imports nothing from a fit/pooling/observables module,
  and ``get_fingerprint`` never computes a value: a miss synthesizes an ``"unresolved"``
  placeholder from ``vocabulary.class_ids`` alone (no observation, no computation), it never
  triggers a fit.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Mapping, Optional

from src.physics.fingerprint.address import RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES, CellAddress
from src.physics.fingerprint.frozen_constants import FINGERPRINT_FROZEN
from src.physics.fingerprint.vocabulary import ClassVocabulary

# Store-format version, recorded on every row so a future schema evolution can branch on it.
FORMAT_VERSION: str = "1"

# Default OWN database path (data artifact, NOT committed, NEVER an f1_data DB). Tests pass
# an explicit temp path (#656).
DEFAULT_DB_PATH: str = "data/driver_fingerprint.db"

_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR: float = float(FINGERPRINT_FROZEN["FINGERPRINT_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR"])

_RESOLVED = "resolved"
_UNRESOLVED = "unresolved"

_COLUMNS = (
    "cell_key", "driver", "era", "vocabulary_version", "class_id", "channel",
    "what_measure", "mean", "sigma", "support_n", "status",
    "shared_floor_applied", "format_version",
)


class EraVocabularyMismatchError(RuntimeError):
    """Raised on any era/vocabulary identity inconsistency -- no silent substitution.

    Covers two distinct cases: (1) the ``era`` argument disagrees with
    ``vocabulary.rules_era`` on a single call; (2) a write targets a
    (driver, era, channel, what_measure) slot that already carries stored cells under a
    DIFFERENT ``vocabulary_version`` (vocabulary drift).
    """


class ReservedWhatMeasureError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a write targets a Build-2 reserved (dormant) ``what_measure`` slot."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CellObservation:
    """One class's observed fit inputs, as passed to :meth:`DriverFingerprintStore.write_fingerprint`.

    ``support_n`` below the pre-registered ``FINGERPRINT_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR`` (or
    ``None``) makes the written cell ``"unresolved"`` regardless of ``mean``/``sigma``.
    """

    mean: Optional[float]
    sigma: Optional[float]
    support_n: Optional[float]
    shared_floor_applied: Optional[bool] = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FingerprintCell:
    """One stored (or synthesized-unresolved) fingerprint cell, as returned by a read."""

    driver: str
    era: str
    vocabulary_version: str
    class_id: str
    channel: str
    what_measure: str
    mean: Optional[float]
    sigma: Optional[float]
    support_n: Optional[float]
    status: str
    shared_floor_applied: Optional[bool]
    format_version: str


class DriverFingerprintStore:
    """SQLite-backed own-DB store of :class:`FingerprintCell` rows.

    Table ``driver_fingerprint_cells``: primary key ``cell_key`` (``NOT NULL``), plus the
    six ``CellAddress`` identity columns, the fitted ``mean``/``sigma``/``support_n``/
    ``shared_floor_applied`` payload, ``status`` (``"resolved"``/``"unresolved"``), and
    ``format_version``.
    """

    def __init__(self, db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH, *, must_exist: bool = False) -> None:
        """Construct the store, creating the schema on first use.

        must_exist:
            When True, raise ``FileNotFoundError`` if ``db_path`` does not already exist,
            BEFORE any connect/schema work -- a read-only construction mode (mirrors
            ``ReferenceUtilizationStore``/``GripStore``).
        """
        if must_exist and not Path(db_path).exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(db_path)
        self.db_path = db_path
        self._init_schema()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ schema
    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        con = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
        con.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        return con

    def _init_schema(self) -> None:
        parent = Path(self.db_path).parent
        if str(parent) not in ("", "."):
            parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        cols_sql = ", ".join(f'"{c}" TEXT NOT NULL' if c == "cell_key" else f'"{c}"' for c in _COLUMNS)
        with self._connect() as con:
            con.execute(
                f"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS driver_fingerprint_cells ({cols_sql}, "
                f'PRIMARY KEY ("cell_key"))'
            )
            self._migrate_missing_columns(con)

    def _migrate_missing_columns(self, con: sqlite3.Connection) -> None:
        """ALTER-add any expected column absent from an existing table (additive only).

        Mirrors the house pattern exactly: a DB created before a new nullable column was
        added keeps loading -- the ADD COLUMN backfills existing rows with NULL rather than
        crashing the query. Never drops or renames.
        """
        existing = {row[1] for row in con.execute("PRAGMA table_info(driver_fingerprint_cells)")}
        for c in _COLUMNS:
            if c not in existing:
                con.execute(f'ALTER TABLE driver_fingerprint_cells ADD COLUMN "{c}"')

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ guards
    def _check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency(self, era: str, vocabulary: ClassVocabulary) -> None:
        if era != vocabulary.rules_era:
            raise EraVocabularyMismatchError(
                f"era={era!r} does not match vocabulary.rules_era={vocabulary.rules_era!r} "
                f"(vocabulary_id={vocabulary.vocabulary_id!r}) -- refusing rather than "
                f"silently choosing one"
            )

    def _check_no_vocabulary_drift(
        self, con: sqlite3.Connection, driver: str, era: str, channel: str, what_measure: str,
        vocabulary: ClassVocabulary,
    ) -> None:
        existing = {
            row[0]
            for row in con.execute(
                "SELECT DISTINCT vocabulary_version FROM driver_fingerprint_cells "
                "WHERE driver=? AND era=? AND channel=? AND what_measure=?",
                (driver, era, channel, what_measure),
            )
        }
        stale = existing - {vocabulary.vocabulary_id}
        if stale:
            raise EraVocabularyMismatchError(
                f"driver={driver!r} era={era!r} channel={channel!r} what_measure={what_measure!r} "
                f"already has stored cells under vocabulary_version(s) {sorted(stale)!r} -- "
                f"refusing to write under a different vocabulary_version "
                f"{vocabulary.vocabulary_id!r} without an explicit migration"
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ write
    def write_fingerprint(
        self,
        driver: str,
        era: str,
        vocabulary: ClassVocabulary,
        channel: str,
        what_measure: str,
        observations: Mapping[str, CellObservation],
        *,
        allow_unverified: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Write EXACTLY ``vocabulary.k`` rows, one per ``vocabulary.class_ids``.

        A class absent from ``observations``, or whose ``support_n`` is below the
        pre-registered unresolved-support floor, is written as ``status="unresolved"``
        (``NULL`` mean/sigma) -- never a missing row. ``INSERT OR REPLACE`` on the
        non-NULL ``cell_key`` primary key makes a rerun idempotent (replace-on-rerun):
        re-writing the same fingerprint never accumulates duplicate rows.
        """
        self._check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency(era, vocabulary)
        if what_measure in RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES:
            raise ReservedWhatMeasureError(
                f"what_measure={what_measure!r} is a reserved (Build-2, dormant) slot -- "
                f"the store refuses to populate it in Build 1"
            )
        vocabulary.require_fittable(override=allow_unverified)

        placeholders = ", ".join("?" for _ in _COLUMNS)
        cols_sql = ", ".join(f'"{c}"' for c in _COLUMNS)
        sql = f"INSERT OR REPLACE INTO driver_fingerprint_cells ({cols_sql}) VALUES ({placeholders})"

        rows: list[tuple] = []
        for class_id in vocabulary.class_ids:
            obs = observations.get(class_id)
            support_n = obs.support_n if obs is not None else None
            is_resolved = (
                obs is not None
                and support_n is not None
                and support_n >= _UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR
            )
            address = CellAddress(
                driver=driver, era=era, vocabulary_version=vocabulary.vocabulary_id,
                class_id=class_id, channel=channel, what_measure=what_measure,
            )
            rows.append(
                (
                    address.cell_key, driver, era, vocabulary.vocabulary_id, class_id, channel,
                    what_measure,
                    (obs.mean if is_resolved else None),
                    (obs.sigma if is_resolved else None),
                    support_n,
                    (_RESOLVED if is_resolved else _UNRESOLVED),
                    (obs.shared_floor_applied if obs is not None else None),
                    FORMAT_VERSION,
                )
            )

        with self._connect() as con:
            self._check_no_vocabulary_drift(con, driver, era, channel, what_measure, vocabulary)
            con.executemany(sql, rows)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ reads
    def get_fingerprint(
        self, driver: str, era: str, vocabulary: ClassVocabulary, channel: str, what_measure: str,
    ) -> list[FingerprintCell]:
        """Return EXACTLY ``vocabulary.k`` cells -- never fits, never omits a class.

        A class with no stored row is synthesized as an ``"unresolved"`` cell purely by
        enumerating ``vocabulary.class_ids`` -- no observation is read, no value is
        computed. This is the NO-fit-on-read guarantee: a miss is a placeholder, not a
        trigger.
        """
        self._check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency(era, vocabulary)
        with self._connect() as con:
            rows = con.execute(
                "SELECT * FROM driver_fingerprint_cells WHERE driver=? AND era=? "
                "AND vocabulary_version=? AND channel=? AND what_measure=?",
                (driver, era, vocabulary.vocabulary_id, channel, what_measure),
            ).fetchall()
        by_class = {r["class_id"]: r for r in rows}

        cells: list[FingerprintCell] = []
        for class_id in vocabulary.class_ids:
            row = by_class.get(class_id)
            if row is None:
                cells.append(
                    FingerprintCell(
                        driver=driver, era=era, vocabulary_version=vocabulary.vocabulary_id,
                        class_id=class_id, channel=channel, what_measure=what_measure,
                        mean=None, sigma=None, support_n=None, status=_UNRESOLVED,
                        shared_floor_applied=None, format_version=FORMAT_VERSION,
                    )
                )
            else:
                cells.append(
                    FingerprintCell(
                        driver=row["driver"], era=row["era"], vocabulary_version=row["vocabulary_version"],
                        class_id=row["class_id"], channel=row["channel"], what_measure=row["what_measure"],
                        mean=row["mean"], sigma=row["sigma"], support_n=row["support_n"],
                        status=row["status"], shared_floor_applied=row["shared_floor_applied"],
                        format_version=row["format_version"],
                    )
                )
        return cells

    def row_count(
        self, driver: str, era: str, vocabulary: ClassVocabulary, channel: str, what_measure: str,
    ) -> int:
        """Number of stored rows for this (driver,era,vocab,channel,what_measure) slot.

        Diagnostic -- used by idempotency tests to confirm a rerun never accumulates
        duplicate rows (expected to equal ``vocabulary.k`` after any number of rewrites).
        """
        with self._connect() as con:
            cur = con.execute(
                "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM driver_fingerprint_cells WHERE driver=? AND era=? "
                "AND vocabulary_version=? AND channel=? AND what_measure=?",
                (driver, era, vocabulary.vocabulary_id, channel, what_measure),
            )
            return int(cur.fetchone()[0])

"""Versioned address space for the DriverFingerprint (issue #666, epic #659, g2).

``CellAddress`` is the SQLite-NULL-PK fix: a frozen dataclass whose ``cell_key``
property is a delimited join of ALL SIX identity fields, validated in
``__post_init__`` to be always non-NULL / non-empty for every component. A
``driver_fingerprint_cells`` row (``store.py``) keys its primary key on this
``cell_key`` and declares it ``NOT NULL`` (belt-and-suspenders): the structural
guarantee lives HERE, in the value object, before any row is ever written.

Two dormant-dimension slots are present-from-day-one, per epic #659 ruling 4
(lowest-dimensionality, dormant slots present-but-unused rather than added
later as a breaking schema change):

* ``channel`` -- Build-1 active values are ``"utilization"`` and ``"energy"``
  (:data:`FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS`); both are FIT axes (see G3, out of scope here).
* ``what_measure`` -- Build-1 default is ``"deficit"`` (:data:`DEFAULT_WHAT_MEASURE`).
  :data:`RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES` are Build-2 race-side slots: a ``CellAddress``
  naming one is CONSTRUCTIBLE (the slot exists), but the store/fit path refuses
  to POPULATE it in Build 1 (that refusal lives in ``store.py``, not here).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, fields

# Delimiter joining the six cell_key components. Chosen because none of the six
# fields (driver code, era key, vocabulary id, class id, channel, what_measure)
# is ever expected to contain a pipe -- and __post_init__ enforces that no
# component may contain it, so a delimiter collision can never silently merge
# two distinct addresses into the same cell_key.
CELL_KEY_DELIMITER: str = "|"

# Build-1 active channel values (both are FIT axes -- see G3). The channel
# dimension itself is present-from-day-one (structural), listed here as the
# single source of the currently-active set.
FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS: tuple[str, ...] = ("utilization", "energy")

# Build-1 default what_measure.
DEFAULT_WHAT_MEASURE: str = "deficit"

# Build-2 race-side what_measure slots: present-but-unused (ruling 4). A
# CellAddress may name one (constructible), but store.py's write path refuses
# to populate it until Build 2 actually implements that semantics.
RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "push",
    "managed",
    "consistency",
    "management_efficiency",
)

_KNOWN_WHAT_MEASURES: frozenset[str] = frozenset((DEFAULT_WHAT_MEASURE,) + RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES)

_CELL_KEY_FIELD_NAMES: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "driver",
    "era",
    "vocabulary_version",
    "class_id",
    "channel",
    "what_measure",
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CellAddress:
    """One fingerprint cell's identity: (driver, era, vocabulary, class, channel, measure).

    Attributes:
        driver: driver code/id.
        era: canonical era key (see ``vocabulary.era_key``); NOT a raw season int.
        vocabulary_version: the ``ClassVocabulary.vocabulary_id`` in force.
        class_id: one of the vocabulary's fully-qualified class labels.
        channel: one of :data:`FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS` (Build-1: both active).
        what_measure: :data:`DEFAULT_WHAT_MEASURE` or a reserved (dormant) slot.

    All six fields are validated non-empty ``str`` with no :data:`CELL_KEY_DELIMITER`
    in ``__post_init__`` -- a ``None``/empty/wrong-type component raises a loud
    ``ValueError`` naming the offending field. This is what makes ``cell_key``
    structurally always non-NULL: the invariant is enforced at construction, not
    merely documented.
    """

    driver: str
    era: str
    vocabulary_version: str
    class_id: str
    channel: str
    what_measure: str

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        for f in fields(self):
            value = getattr(self, f.name)
            if not isinstance(value, str) or value == "":
                raise ValueError(
                    f"CellAddress.{f.name}: expected a non-empty str, got {value!r}"
                )
            if CELL_KEY_DELIMITER in value:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"CellAddress.{f.name}: value {value!r} contains the reserved "
                    f"cell_key delimiter {CELL_KEY_DELIMITER!r}"
                )
        if self.what_measure not in _KNOWN_WHAT_MEASURES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"CellAddress.what_measure: expected one of "
                f"{sorted(_KNOWN_WHAT_MEASURES)}, got {self.what_measure!r}"
            )

    @property
    def cell_key(self) -> str:
        """Delimited join of all six identity fields -- always non-NULL, non-empty."""
        return CELL_KEY_DELIMITER.join(getattr(self, name) for name in _CELL_KEY_FIELD_NAMES)

    @property
    def is_reserved_what_measure(self) -> bool:
        """True when ``what_measure`` is a dormant Build-2 slot, not the Build-1 default."""
        return self.what_measure in RESERVED_WHAT_MEASURES

"""#675 class-axis coverage diagnostic: does the driver x class two-way `predictive_t`
interval under-cover on the CLASS axis on REAL bounded-slice support, and does that
under-coverage generalize across BOTH channels (time, energy)?

Epic #659 gate 666-g1-implement (research diagnostic; test-after/inspection per the
handoff test mode -- NOT promoted logic). See
``.agent-work/666-driver-fingerprint/crew-handoffs/g1-implement-handoff.md`` for the
full pre-registered coverage method this module pins EXACTLY.

## Why this exists

The G3 fit needs to know whether to apply a class-level `shared_floor` (#627 G4,
`pool_random_effects`) on top of the driver x class two-way decomposition. That decision
must rest on a POWERED, non-circular coverage measurement -- not eyeballing one fit on
one real (tiny) slice. This module reproduces #665's synthetic-recovery method
(``scripts/pooling_imbalance_validation_665.py``, READ-ONLY, not edited here) but swaps
#665's PROXY class-share profiles for the REAL per-(driver, class) support counts read
from the commander-provided bounded slice DB -- the actual imbalance the G3 fit will see.

## Method (PRIMARY verdict)

For each channel (`time`: `time_deficit_s`, `energy`: `deployment_share`) and axis
(`driver`, `class`):

1. Real per-(driver, class) SUPPORT COUNTS: `n_points` summed across the 4 circuits in
   the slice (the actual cell imbalance the G3 fit sees). A cell whose summed support
   falls below ``FINGERPRINT_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR`` (pre-registered, #666
   ``frozen_constants.py``) is `unresolved` and excluded (no synthetic draws for it --
   same "legitimate empty cell" convention #665 uses for a `n <= 0` cell).
2. Generative model (#665's, reused verbatim in structure):
   `y[d,c] = grand_mean + true_driver_effect[d] + true_class_effect[c] + N(0, obs_sigma)`,
   fresh `true_driver_effect ~ N(0, driver_sigma)` / `true_class_effect ~ N(0,
   class_sigma)` drawn each repetition. TIME-channel sigmas are #665's own constants
   verbatim (`driver_sigma=0.15, class_sigma=0.30, obs_sigma=1.0`). ENERGY-channel sigmas
   are these same three values scaled by ``ENERGY_SCALE`` -- see "Energy-channel sigma
   derivation" below (an implementer choice, per the handoff's Authority section; NOT
   commander-pre-registered).
3. `fit_two_way(values, teams=drivers, circuits=classes)` -- UNMODIFIED import from
   `src.physics.layer2.pooling` (never edited by this module). Each shrunk axis effect is
   wrapped in `predictive_t(eff, sem, n_eff, nu_loss=4.0, rule=FormulaRule())` where `sem`
   is the naive (unshrunk) within-group SEM (`fit_two_way` exposes no per-effect sigma of
   its own -- same companion-sigma construction #665 uses) and `n_eff` is the SUMMED REAL
   observation count backing that axis estimate (driver: sum over that driver's resolved
   cells; class: sum over that class's resolved cells) -- **never** `fit_two_way`'s own
   `.n` (a total-row count, not a per-axis effective count; #665's exact subtlety).
4. `lo, hi = pt.interval(FINGERPRINT_NOMINAL_COVERAGE_LEVEL)` (0.80); `hit = int(lo <=
   true_val <= hi)`. Accumulated over `N_REPS >= 200` repetitions x every entity present
   in that repetition, per axis per channel.
5. Empirical coverage = hits / n, reported WITH a Clopper-Pearson exact 95% binomial CI
   (so the `generalizes` flag below does not flip on sampling noise alone).

`generalizes` (per channel) = `true` iff the CLASS axis's coverage-CI **upper** bound is
below `FINGERPRINT_UNDER_COVERAGE_BOUND` (0.60, pre-registered) -- i.e. we are 95%-confident
the true class-axis coverage sits below the gating bound, not merely that the point
estimate does.

## Energy-channel sigma derivation (implementer choice, stated per the handoff)

`ENERGY_SCALE = std(deployment_share) / std(time_deficit_s)` computed from the REAL slice
rows (severity classes only) -- preserves the SAME relative structure #665 uses

305	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 5. Public entry point
306	def fit_driver_fingerprints(
307	    observables_db_path: str,
308	    store: DriverFingerprintStore,
309	    driver: str,
310	    *,
311	    as_of_round: int,
312	    era: str,
313	    vocabulary: ClassVocabulary,
314	    season: int,
315	    session_type: str = "Q",
316	    map_version: Optional[str] = None,
317	    channels: Sequence[str] = FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS,
318	    what_measure: str = DEFAULT_WHAT_MEASURE,
319	    allow_unverified: bool = False,
320	) -> Mapping[str, Mapping[str, CellObservation]]:
321	    """Fit one driver's fingerprint cells (both channels) as-of ``as_of_round`` and write
322	    them into ``store``.
323	
324	    ``as_of_round`` is keyword-only with NO default -- a call that omits it raises
325	    ``TypeError`` from Python's own argument binding, before a single line of this function
326	    body runs (crown invariant "as_of_round REQUIRED no default").
327	
328	    Refuses via ``vocabulary.require_fittable()`` unless the taxonomy's F12 verdict is
329	    ``"PASS"`` (or ``allow_unverified=True``), mirroring ``store.write_fingerprint``'s own
330	    refusal. Writes exactly ``vocabulary.k`` cells per channel via
331	    ``store.write_fingerprint`` -- a class with no in-cutoff support (or below the
332	    pre-registered support floor) is written ``"unresolved"`` by the store itself, never a
333	    missing row.
334	
335	    Returns the RESOLVED observations actually computed per channel (a diagnostic /
336	    test-facing return value; the store write is the durable side effect).
337	    """
338	    vocabulary.require_fittable(override=allow_unverified)
339	
340	    rows = _read_observable_rows(
341	        observables_db_path, season=season, session_type=session_type,
342	        map_version=map_version, as_of_round=as_of_round,
343	    )
344	
345	    written: dict[str, dict[str, CellObservation]] = {}
346	    for channel in channels:
347	        if channel not in _VALUE_COLUMN_BY_CHANNEL:
348	            raise ValueError(
349	                f"channel: expected one of {sorted(_VALUE_COLUMN_BY_CHANNEL)}, got {channel!r}"
350	            )
351	        observations = _fit_channel(
352	            rows, channel, driver=driver, as_of_round=as_of_round,
353	            halflife_rounds=_RECENCY_HALFLIFE_ROUNDS, unresolved_floor=_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR,
354	            class_ids=vocabulary.class_ids,
355	        )
356	        store.write_fingerprint(
357	            driver, era, vocabulary, channel, what_measure, observations,
358	            allow_unverified=allow_unverified,
359	        )
360	        written[channel] = observations
361	    return written

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 5. Public entry point
def fit_driver_fingerprints(
    observables_db_path: str,
    store: DriverFingerprintStore,
    driver: str,
    *,
    as_of_round: int,
    era: str,
    vocabulary: ClassVocabulary,
    season: int,
    session_type: str = "Q",
    map_version: Optional[str] = None,
    channels: Sequence[str] = FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS,
    what_measure: str = DEFAULT_WHAT_MEASURE,
    allow_unverified: bool = False,
) -> Mapping[str, Mapping[str, CellObservation]]:
    """Fit one driver's fingerprint cells (both channels) as-of ``as_of_round`` and write
    them into ``store``.

    ``as_of_round`` is keyword-only with NO default -- a call that omits it raises
    ``TypeError`` from Python's own argument binding, before a single line of this function
    body runs (crown invariant "as_of_round REQUIRED no default").

    Refuses via ``vocabulary.require_fittable()`` unless the taxonomy's F12 verdict is
    ``"PASS"`` (or ``allow_unverified=True``), mirroring ``store.write_fingerprint``'s own
    refusal. Writes exactly ``vocabulary.k`` cells per channel via
    ``store.write_fingerprint`` -- a class with no in-cutoff support (or below the
    pre-registered support floor) is written ``"unresolved"`` by the store itself, never a
    missing row.

    Returns the RESOLVED observations actually computed per channel (a diagnostic /
    test-facing return value; the store write is the durable side effect).
    """
    vocabulary.require_fittable(override=allow_unverified)

    rows = _read_observable_rows(
        observables_db_path, season=season, session_type=session_type,
        map_version=map_version, as_of_round=as_of_round,
    )

    written: dict[str, dict[str, CellObservation]] = {}
    for channel in channels:
        if channel not in _VALUE_COLUMN_BY_CHANNEL:
            raise ValueError(
                f"channel: expected one of {sorted(_VALUE_COLUMN_BY_CHANNEL)}, got {channel!r}"
            )
        observations = _fit_channel(
            rows, channel, driver=driver, as_of_round=as_of_round,
            halflife_rounds=_RECENCY_HALFLIFE_ROUNDS, unresolved_floor=_UNRESOLVED_SUPPORT_FLOOR,
            class_ids=vocabulary.class_ids,
        )
        store.write_fingerprint(
            driver, era, vocabulary, channel, what_measure, observations,
            allow_unverified=allow_unverified,
        )
        written[channel] = observations
    return written

# Constellation Interrogator

Resolve the handed-in goal to common understanding through relentless, one-question-at-a-time interrogation. Whoever handed you the goal is your **counterpart** — most often a dispatching delegate (a Commander running under an Admiral launch order, or any delegated dispatch), sometimes a human at the keyboard. Walk the design tree, resolving dependencies one at a time; for each question give a recommended answer. If you're given a list of questions, treat it as a prompt, not a script: decide your own initial question set, and don't let an over-prescribed seed shortcut your framing.

Frame an ambiguous ask in behavior terms first. Start from the capability, then drill: **what capability is being added or changed** (the present-tense thing the system will do); **concrete examples/use cases** of that capability in action, including the edge cases; **events that matter** architecturally (boundary-crossing or contract signals, not every runtime event); and the **governing rules/constraints/assumptions**. Resolve which capability is in play before debating mechanism. Map this framing to the existing `capability`/`event`/`constraint`/`assumption` ontology so the resolved understanding hands cleanly to the Cartographer.

## Start here — drive the engine before you touch the question

You were handed a goal to resolve, not to answer from assumption. The moment this skill loads — before you frame a single question — do this, in order:

1. **Build the survey and CLAIM the engine lease.** Instantiate your `survey` from `templates/INTERROGATION.template.json`, then `claim` the checklist lease with the engine. This is your **first command**, ahead of any framing.
2. **Ask the engine what to do next, at every question.** Run the engine's `current` verb, do exactly what the active question's imperative says, and `advance`/`skip` only once its postconditions pass. Never skip ahead, and never hand-write or hand-edit the survey file — the engine owns that state and stamps the provenance (session lease, heartbeats, evidence) that proves the interrogation was really driven.
3. **Resolving one question is the MIDDLE of the survey, not the end.** Recording one answer is not done — integrate it, `advance` that question, then drive every remaining question and branch through the engine to a consolidated understanding. **Do not end your turn while any question is still `pending` or `in-progress`:** run the engine's `current` verb and keep going until it reports the survey is done. The single most common failure at this tier is stopping the moment one answer lands — resist it. Run the engine's final `advance`/`consolidate` first, and **only then** `release` the engine session lease as your very last action. Releasing before that closing advance fails the terminal provenance check — the lease must cover every journaled action.
4. **Waiting on your counterpart is never a reason to end your turn.** If you must reconcile a question against a frozen launch order or a dispatching delegate rather than a live human, resolve it **actively, inside your turn**: read the order, `skip` what it settles, and continue the survey; only a genuine gap goes up as a context query or float. Treat the thought "I'll wait for an answer" as the cue to **resolve from the order and keep going**, never to stop and yield.

**Work the engine never saw did not happen.** A survey that resolves the goal directly, or copies the survey template and never advances it, or hand-writes a survey that merely *looks* complete, or **drives the engine only as far as one answer and then stops**, has **failed this dispatch** no matter how correct the answer — the deliverable of an Interrogator run is a survey driven all the way to a consolidated understanding. Report a proof-of-life as soon as you start.

Compliance/engine-drive rule: inherited — see `references/global-everyone.md`.

Drive the question list as a `survey` from `templates/INTERROGATION.template.json` through the absolute path to this installed skill's bundled engine (`scripts/checklist_engine.py`, workbench `references/checklist-engine.md`): ask one question at a time and resolve its answer; `append` follow-ups and new branches as answers open them; `skip` questions an earlier answer settled; then `consolidate` into the resolved understanding.

## Facts vs. decisions — resolve one, block on the other

Type every question **`fact`** or **`decision`** — this sharpens the code-answers-over-questions doctrine, it does not add a rule.
- A **fact** is answerable from the codebase: resolve it yourself and record the code evidence.
- A **decision** is a choice your counterpart owns: **never self-answer it** — block and take it to them (a delegated float beyond your latitude, a direct question to a live human).

The rail (`scripts/verify_interrogation.py`) refuses a resolved `decision` with no human answer and a resolved `fact` with no code evidence, so the split can't be quietly collapsed.

**Where the answer comes from (two modes).** *Delegated* (the common case — no reachable human): your counterpart is the **frozen launch order / dispatching delegate**. Answer each question from it, `skip` questions it already settles, and when it neither answers nor lets you safely proceed, take it **to the delegate** — a missing fact as a **context query**, a choice outside inherited latitude as a **float** — rather than blocking on an absent human. *Interactive* (a human is at the keyboard — e.g. the Admiral's own latitude interrogation): ask the human directly and **wait for the answer**.

## While interrogating
- Ask one question at a time.
- Challenge terms that conflict with the glossary; propose a precise canonical term for vague or overloaded ones.
- Stress-test domain relationships with concrete edge-case scenarios.
- Cross-check claims against the code and surface contradictions.

## Finish gate — joint understanding, not a terminated loop

The loop running out of questions is **not** the end; **joint understanding** is. Before you consolidate, capture an explicit **sign-off** from your counterpart that questioning is complete and the understanding is shared — not a token you stamp yourself. Record the run to `templates/INTERROGATION_RECORD.template.json`, run `scripts/verify_interrogation.py <record>` (it refuses consolidation without the sign-off), and `consolidate` only once it exits 0. An async counterpart's exception needs an **independent reviewer's** co-sign + log, never your own.

Keep going until joint understanding is signed off or your counterpart says enough, then consolidate the result for the invoker.

Templates: `templates/INTERROGATION.template.json`, `templates/INTERROGATION_RECORD.template.json`. Rail: `scripts/verify_interrogation.py`. Reference: workbench `references/checklist-engine.md`.

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Refuse a self-answered or unsigned interrogation — the interrogator RAIL.

This is the mechanically-enforced rail for the `constellation-interrogator`
sharpening (DESIGN_SPEC Section D1). The interrogator drives a survey to a joint
understanding; this script is the gate the interrogation RECORD must clear before
that understanding may be called consolidated. It enforces the two locked
behaviors in code, so neither can rest on the agent's self-assertion:

  * FACTS-VS-DECISIONS SPLIT. Every question is typed `fact` or `decision`. A
    `fact` is a question the agent may resolve by exploring the codebase; a
    `decision` is a genuine choice that must block on the human/counterpart.
      - A `decision` marked `resolved` MUST carry a non-empty `human_answer` —
        a decision is NEVER self-answered by the agent (the DECISION-BLOCK).
      - A `fact` marked `resolved` MUST carry non-empty `code_evidence` — a
        resolved fact is grounded in code/docs, not asserted (the split's other
        edge). A resolved fact needs NO human answer; that is what "allowed" means.

  * NO-QUIT-EARLY FINISH GATE. A record marked `consolidated: true` MUST carry a
    joint-understanding `signoff` — a real human exchange with a non-empty `by`
    AND `statement` — AND no question may still be `open`. Loop termination is not
    the gate; the explicit sign-off that questioning is complete is. Absent it,
    consolidation is REFUSED.

A defended exception to the finish gate (e.g. an async counterpart) requires a
`rail_exception` carrying a non-empty `reviewer_cosign` (the INDEPENDENT reviewer,
never the author) AND a non-empty `log` entry — self-assertion never passes. The
exception covers the finish gate ONLY; it never excuses a self-answered decision.

Everything else — whether the questioning actually dug deep, whether the recorded
understanding is right — is the INDEPENDENT reviewer's judgment (DESIGN_SPEC TF8),
deliberately NOT gated here. Standard library only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

VALID_MODES = ("delegated", "interactive")
VALID_KINDS = ("fact", "decision")
VALID_STATUSES = ("resolved", "open", "skipped")


class InterrogationError(Exception):
    """Raised when an interrogation record fails the rail — the refusal."""


def _require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise InterrogationError(message)


def _nonempty(value: object) -> bool:
    return bool(str(value).strip()) if value is not None else False

# Mission Frame — cmdr-698 (issue #698)

Map input: `docs/architecture/index.md` (orientation RESOLVED, 76 anchors, receipt
`.agent-work/cmdr-698/map-orientation.json`). Packet read: `docs/architecture/packets/physics.md`,
fingerprint section. Problem statement: `.agent-work/cmdr-698/INTERROGATION_RECORD.json`
(11/11 questions resolved, rail exit 0).

**This frame is required, not shrunk.** The issue reads as three one-liners, but the map places
H1 squarely inside a component that four other landed stages consume, and interrogation found
two of the issue's three stated premises to be factually wrong. A trivial-change frame would
have carried both errors into the gate plan.

---

## Intent

Harden three loose edges left by #666 (DriverFingerprint, epic #659 stage G) without changing
any fit or coverage behaviour:

- **H1** — the `DriverFingerprintStore` read/write surface takes four bare strings plus a
  vocabulary object. Give it a validated value object so a malformed address cannot reach SQL.
- **H2** — `scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py` has no worktree-first `sys.path` guard,
  so a bare run inside a git worktree silently imports the MAIN checkout's `src/`.
- **H3** — the coverage / bounded-fit JSON artifacts are, contrary to the issue's assumption,
  **not** gitignored while a work area is live.

Present-tense capability being changed: *persisting and reading one driver's fingerprint cells
for a (driver, era, vocabulary, channel, measure) slot* — the address it is asked for becomes a
validated value rather than four unchecked strings. No stored value, no fit, and no coverage
number changes.

## Corrections to the issue text (load-bearing)

The issue is right that a defect exists in all three places, but three of its specifics are wrong
and the plan is built on the corrected reading:

1. **H1's premise is false.** "the `CellAddress` value object the fit layer already uses" — the
   fit layer does **not** use `CellAddress`. It appears only inside `store.py` (import + one
   internal construction) and its own unit test; `fit.py` passes the same loose primitives the
   issue objects to.
2. **H1's acceptance is unbuildable as literally written.** "store API typed on `CellAddress`"
   cannot be done: a `CellAddress` names **one cell** (it carries `class_id`), while every store
   method names a whole **k-class slot** and loops over `vocabulary.class_ids` internally. The
   buildable form is a new `FingerprintSlot` value object (= `CellAddress` minus `class_id`),
   with `CellAddress` retained as its per-cell derivation.
3. **H3's assumption is false.** The artifacts are *not* "already ignored via `.agent-work/`" —
   there is no blanket `.agent-work/` rule in `.gitignore`; only `*.pkl` / `*.npz` / `*.db` /
   `scratch/` / `ckpt/` / `backtests/` and a few named record dirs. The archived twins are in
   fact **tracked in git**. H3 therefore widens from a no-op confirmation to a real rule.

## Affected capabilities

- Fingerprint cell persistence and read-back (`struct:physics.fingerprint`, `store.py`) — the
  only capability whose *interface* changes. Its four structural guarantees (non-NULL
  `cell_key`, k-cells-always-populated, loud refusal / no silent substitution, no fit-on-read)
  must survive byte-for-byte in behaviour.
- Stage-G fingerprint fitting (`struct:physics.fingerprint`, `fit.py`) — call-site only; its
  public signature is deliberately unchanged (see decision pressure below).
- End-to-end pilot orchestration (`struct:physics.pilot`) — call-site only, two `get_fingerprint`
  reads.
- Local diagnostic/reproduction runs of the #675 coverage script and the artifact hygiene of a
  live work area — no runtime capability, but both are how a future worktree run is reproduced.

## Structural anchors

- `struct:physics.fingerprint` — the component that owns the change (`src/physics/fingerprint/`:
  `address.py`, `store.py`, `fit.py`).
- `struct:physics.pilot` — downstream consumer, two `get_fingerprint` call sites.
- `struct:physics.instrument_panel` — **adjacent but not a consumer**: it imports only
  `FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS` from `address.py`, never the store. Verified, so it stays out of scope.
- `struct:physics.layer2.pooling` — reused by `fit.py`, untouched here; named so the gate does
  not drift into it.
- `struct:physics` / `struct:utils` — region boundary and the `simplification_limits` checker
  the project requires on touched Python paths.

## Relevant examples / edge cases

- A caller passes `era=""` or `driver=None`: today it reaches a parameterised `SELECT`/`INSERT`
  and returns or writes nothing loudly wrong. After the change it raises at slot construction.
- A caller passes a value containing the `|` `CELL_KEY_DELIMITER`: today two distinct addresses
  could collide into one `cell_key`; the value object already refuses this for cells and must
  refuse it for slots.
- A caller passes an unknown `what_measure`: today `store.write_fingerprint` refuses only the
  *reserved* Build-2 slots; an outright unknown string is refused only later, inside the per-class
  `CellAddress` construction. The slot moves that refusal to the boundary.
- `era` disagreeing with `vocabulary.rules_era`: must **still** raise `EraVocabularyMismatchError`.
  This is the one place the tightening could quietly delete a documented refusal, and it must not.
- A reserved Build-2 `what_measure` is still *constructible* and refused only on write — that
  asymmetry is deliberate and preserved.

## Architecturally meaningful events

- `EraVocabularyMismatchError` on argument inconsistency and on vocabulary drift — a
  boundary-crossing refusal signal other stages rely on.
- `ReservedWhatMeasureError` on a Build-2 dormant slot write.
- `ValueError` from the address/slot value object — the new, earlier failure signal this issue
  exists to create.

## Governing constraints and assumptions

- `constraint:physics_region_no_evo_import` — nothing in this change may import evo /
  `latent_power` / `compound_prior`. Verified none of the touched files does today.
- One canonical path, no compatibility shims or dual-format boundary acceptance
  (`docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md`; `docs/agents/engine-config.json` `rules_root`). This is why the
  store signature change is **breaking**, with every call site migrated in the same gate, rather
  than an additive overload.
- Evidence requirements (`docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md`): `py -m
  src.utils.simplification_limits` on touched `src/` and `tests/` paths; test-led change with the
  focused physics-region suite green.
- Issue-stated exclusion: **no behaviour change to the fit or the coverage computation**.
- Assumption carried forward from the archived #666 run and re-verified here: `data/driver_fingerprint.db`
  is an own-DB artifact, never an `f1_data*.db`; nothing in this change touches DB content or schema.

## Decision anchors and decision pressure

Existing anchors this change sits next to (read-only, none revised):

- `decision:join-consumer-boundary` — the race sim and the panel read un-aggregated cells
  directly. It is why the store's read surface has more consumers than the join does, and why a
  breaking read signature has to be migrated rather than shimmed.
- `claim:instrument_panel_reads_cells_directly` — the claim that keeps `instrument_panel` out of
  this change's blast radius; re-verified (it imports `FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS` only).

# Plan-alternatives + cold critic — cmdr-698

Both rigor mechanisms are bias-to-yes. Both were **run**, and both were run in a **weakened
form**; the weakening is named below as an untaken road rather than hidden.

## Untaken road (applies to both mechanisms)

The engagement brief forbids dispatching subagents unless the principal asks for them, and the
principal did not. So the alternatives were **authored by one mind, not N parallel independent
authors**, and the critic pass is an **adversarial self-read, not an independent cold reader with
no authoring context**. That is a real loss: a self-critic cannot be surprised by its own framing.
Panel-vs-single is therefore not a scaling choice I made — it was constrained to single. If the
principal wants the genuine article on return, the cheap version is one cold critic dispatched
against `MISSION_FRAME.md` + `execute.json` alone, ~one agent.

---

## Plan-alternatives — three candidates under distinct constraints

### Candidate A — minimum blast radius (constraint: touch the fewest files, fewest gates)
- **G1**: everything H1 (mint the slot, retype the store, migrate all call sites, new tests).
- **G2**: H2 + H3.
- 2 gates.

### Candidate B — risk-ordered, cheap-first (constraint: every gate boundary independently green, and a stall on the risky item must not strand the trivial ones)
- **G1**: H2 (`sys.path` guard) + H3 (`.gitignore` rule) — zero-logic, one line each, verified by
  cheap mechanical checks.
- **G2**: H1 — the slot value object, the store retype, the call-site migration, the tests.
- 2 gates, reversed order.

### Candidate C — value-object-first / strict TDD (constraint: the new type lands proven before any consumer churn)
- **G1**: mint + fully test `FingerprintSlot` alone.
- **G2**: retype the store, migrate the ~50 call sites.
- **G3**: H2 + H3.
- 3 gates.

### Comparison

| axis | A | B | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| depth (behaviour per unit of interface learned) | same | same | same |
| locality | poor — the risky change is bundled first, so any rework re-opens the trivia behind it | **good** — each gate is one concern with its own cheap verification | good |
| seam placement | identical in all three (the store boundary) | identical | identical |
| testability | fine | fine | best in principle | 
| failure behaviour | a BLOCK on H1 review strands H2/H3 behind it | **a BLOCK on H1 leaves H2/H3 already landed and green** | same as B but slower |
| gate-boundary health | fine | fine | **G1 ships an unconsumed class — a reviewer will correctly flag dead code at the boundary** |

### Converged recommendation: **B, with C's discipline folded inside G2**

B wins on failure behaviour and locality: the two zero-risk items land first and cost a reviewer
almost nothing, and the one genuinely risky change is isolated so its rework touches nothing else.
C's real virtue — write the value object and its tests before the store depends on it — is kept,
but *inside* G2 as an ordering instruction rather than as its own gate, because a gate boundary
that ships a class with no consumer is a code smell a reviewer has to argue past. A is rejected:
it inverts B's ordering for no gain.

This is a recommendation, not a menu: **B+C-inside-G2** is the plan authored into `execute.json`.

---

## Cold plan critic — adversarial read of the converged plan + mission frame

Eight findings. Six were folded into the gate plan; two are accepted risks recorded here.

1. **"`FingerprintSlot` will duplicate `CellAddress`'s validation, and the two copies will drift."**
   *Valid.* Folded in: G2's imperative requires the per-field validation (non-empty `str`, no
   `CELL_KEY_DELIMITER`) to be factored into **one** shared private helper in `address.py` used by
   both classes, not copy-pasted.
2. **"Does `row_count` get the slot too, or is the tightening partial?"**
   *Valid and easy to miss* — `row_count` takes the same five primitives. Folded in: G2 names all
   **three** methods explicitly (`write_fingerprint`, `get_fingerprint`, `row_count`); a partial
   retype fails the gate.
3. **"~45 test call sites is a large mechanical diff — a weakened assertion could ride in unnoticed."**
   *Valid.* Folded in: G2's review criteria require the reviewer to confirm no pre-existing
   assertion was weakened or deleted, only its call form changed; and the module's own
   pre-existing tests must pass (`lesson:consumed-frozen-module-run-guard-tests`).
4. **"`address.py` grows ~40 lines — does it still clear `simplification_limits`?"**
   *Valid.* Folded in: `simplification_limits` on the touched paths is a G2 closeout postcondition,
   not an afterthought.
5. **"The `.gitignore` rule could hide evidence a future commander legitimately wants to commit."**
   *Accepted risk, mitigated.* The archive path stays trackable by construction, which is exactly
   the repo's own rule ("commit Commander work logs only after the work package is archived under
   `.agent-work/archive`"). Folded in: the rule must carry an explanatory comment naming that intent,
   so the next reader does not delete it as mysterious.
6. **"`git check-ignore` was never actually run this session — the H3 finding rests on reading
   `.gitignore`, not on the tool."**
   *Valid and important.* Folded in: G1's closeout postcondition **runs** `git check-ignore` on both
   a live path and the tracked archive path. The planning-time finding is treated as a strong
   inference to be confirmed, not as a closed fact.
7. **"Does `.agent-work/*/artifacts/*.json` cover nested work-ids like `epic-659/665`?"**

   Recorded in the frame's Out-of-scope and carried as a triage candidate rather than silently
   widening the rule (widening it is precisely what would shadow the archive).
8. **"An inserted `sys.path` guard is inert if it lands after the `from src...` imports."**
   *Valid.* Folded in: the H2 acceptance is an **ordering** property — guard before the first `src.`
   import — and G1's check asserts the order, not merely the presence of the line.

**Accepted risks (not fixed, stated):** (a) the critic was not independent — see the untaken road
above; (b) the worktree failure H2 describes cannot be *reproduced* from the main checkout, because
the editable-install `.pth` makes `src` importable there regardless, so G1 verifies the invariant
(guard-before-import) rather than the symptom.

# Plan-alternatives + cold critic — cmdr-698

Both rigor mechanisms are bias-to-yes. Both were **run**, and both were run in a **weakened
form**; the weakening is named below as an untaken road rather than hidden.

## Untaken road (applies to both mechanisms)

The engagement brief forbids dispatching subagents unless the principal asks for them, and the
principal did not. So the alternatives were **authored by one mind, not N parallel independent
authors**, and the critic pass is an **adversarial self-read, not an independent cold reader with
no authoring context**. That is a real loss: a self-critic cannot be surprised by its own framing.
Panel-vs-single is therefore not a scaling choice I made — it was constrained to single. If the
principal wants the genuine article on return, the cheap version is one cold critic dispatched
against `MISSION_FRAME.md` + `execute.json` alone, ~one agent.

---

## Plan-alternatives — three candidates under distinct constraints

### Candidate A — minimum blast radius (constraint: touch the fewest files, fewest gates)
- **G1**: everything H1 (mint the slot, retype the store, migrate all call sites, new tests).
- **G2**: H2 + H3.
- 2 gates.

### Candidate B — risk-ordered, cheap-first (constraint: every gate boundary independently green, and a stall on the risky item must not strand the trivial ones)
- **G1**: H2 (`sys.path` guard) + H3 (`.gitignore` rule) — zero-logic, one line each, verified by
  cheap mechanical checks.
- **G2**: H1 — the slot value object, the store retype, the call-site migration, the tests.
- 2 gates, reversed order.

### Candidate C — value-object-first / strict TDD (constraint: the new type lands proven before any consumer churn)
- **G1**: mint + fully test `FingerprintSlot` alone.
- **G2**: retype the store, migrate the ~50 call sites.
- **G3**: H2 + H3.
- 3 gates.

### Comparison

| axis | A | B | C |
|---|---|---|---|
| depth (behaviour per unit of interface learned) | same | same | same |
| locality | poor — the risky change is bundled first, so any rework re-opens the trivia behind it | **good** — each gate is one concern with its own cheap verification | good |
| seam placement | identical in all three (the store boundary) | identical | identical |
| testability | fine | fine | best in principle | 
| failure behaviour | a BLOCK on H1 review strands H2/H3 behind it | **a BLOCK on H1 leaves H2/H3 already landed and green** | same as B but slower |
| gate-boundary health | fine | fine | **G1 ships an unconsumed class — a reviewer will correctly flag dead code at the boundary** |

### Converged recommendation: **B, with C's discipline folded inside G2**

B wins on failure behaviour and locality: the two zero-risk items land first and cost a reviewer
almost nothing, and the one genuinely risky change is isolated so its rework touches nothing else.
C's real virtue — write the value object and its tests before the store depends on it — is kept,
but *inside* G2 as an ordering instruction rather than as its own gate, because a gate boundary
that ships a class with no consumer is a code smell a reviewer has to argue past. A is rejected:
it inverts B's ordering for no gain.

This is a recommendation, not a menu: **B+C-inside-G2** is the plan authored into `execute.json`.

---

## Cold plan critic — adversarial read of the converged plan + mission frame

Eight findings. Six were folded into the gate plan; two are accepted risks recorded here.

1. **"`FingerprintSlot` will duplicate `CellAddress`'s validation, and the two copies will drift."**
   *Valid.* Folded in: G2's imperative requires the per-field validation (non-empty `str`, no
   `CELL_KEY_DELIMITER`) to be factored into **one** shared private helper in `address.py` used by
   both classes, not copy-pasted.
2. **"Does `row_count` get the slot too, or is the tightening partial?"**
   *Valid and easy to miss* — `row_count` takes the same five primitives. Folded in: G2 names all
   **three** methods explicitly (`write_fingerprint`, `get_fingerprint`, `row_count`); a partial
   retype fails the gate.
3. **"~45 test call sites is a large mechanical diff — a weakened assertion could ride in unnoticed."**
   *Valid.* Folded in: G2's review criteria require the reviewer to confirm no pre-existing
   assertion was weakened or deleted, only its call form changed; and the module's own
   pre-existing tests must pass (`lesson:consumed-frozen-module-run-guard-tests`).
4. **"`address.py` grows ~40 lines — does it still clear `simplification_limits`?"**
   *Valid.* Folded in: `simplification_limits` on the touched paths is a G2 closeout postcondition,
   not an afterthought.
5. **"The `.gitignore` rule could hide evidence a future commander legitimately wants to commit."**
   *Accepted risk, mitigated.* The archive path stays trackable by construction, which is exactly
   the repo's own rule ("commit Commander work logs only after the work package is archived under
   `.agent-work/archive`"). Folded in: the rule must carry an explanatory comment naming that intent,
   so the next reader does not delete it as mysterious.
6. **"`git check-ignore` was never actually run this session — the H3 finding rests on reading
   `.gitignore`, not on the tool."**
   *Valid and important.* Folded in: G1's closeout postcondition **runs** `git check-ignore` on both
   a live path and the tracked archive path. The planning-time finding is treated as a strong
   inference to be confirmed, not as a closed fact.
7. **"Does `.agent-work/*/artifacts/*.json` cover nested work-ids like `epic-659/665`?"**
   *Valid — it does not.* A nested work-id puts `artifacts/` two segments deep, outside the glob.
   Recorded in the frame's Out-of-scope and carried as a triage candidate rather than silently
   widening the rule (widening it is precisely what would shadow the archive).
8. **"An inserted `sys.path` guard is inert if it lands after the `from src...` imports."**
   *Valid.* Folded in: the H2 acceptance is an **ordering** property — guard before the first `src.`
   import — and G1's check asserts the order, not merely the presence of the line.

9. **"H2 widens to a second script the issue never named — that is scope creep on a
   recommend-and-defer issue."**
   *Valid as a concern, overruled on balance, and the overrule is recorded.* `scripts/pooling_imbalance_validation_665.py`
   is the only other epic-#659 fingerprint-family script missing the guard, carries the identical
   3-line fix with zero behaviour change, and is the methodological twin #675 cites in its own
   docstring — a worktree run that trips one trips the other on the next command. Folded in: capped at
   **one** named file, given its **own** attestable close criterion inside G1 so the owner can drop it
   without disturbing the rest of the gate, and named explicitly in the PR body. Explicitly **not**
   widened to the ~26 other repo scripts lacking the guard → triage.

# Mission Frame — cmdr-698 (issue #698)

Map input: `docs/architecture/index.md` (orientation RESOLVED, 76 anchors, receipt
`.agent-work/cmdr-698/map-orientation.json`). Packet read: `docs/architecture/packets/physics.md`,
fingerprint section. Problem statement: `.agent-work/cmdr-698/PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md` +
`.agent-work/cmdr-698/INTERROGATION_RECORD.json` (12/12 questions resolved, rail exit 0).

**This frame is required, not shrunk.** The issue reads as three one-liners, but the map places
H1 squarely inside a component that four other landed stages consume, and interrogation found
two of the issue's three stated premises to be factually wrong. A trivial-change frame would
have carried both errors into the gate plan.

---

## Intent

Harden three loose edges left by #666 (DriverFingerprint, epic #659 stage G) without changing
any fit or coverage behaviour:

- **H1** — the `DriverFingerprintStore` read/write surface takes four bare strings plus a
  vocabulary object. Give it a validated value object so a malformed address cannot reach SQL.
- **H2** — `scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py` has no worktree-first `sys.path` guard,
  so a bare run inside a git worktree silently imports the MAIN checkout's `src/`.
- **H3** — the coverage / bounded-fit JSON artifacts are, contrary to the issue's assumption,
  **not** gitignored while a work area is live.

Present-tense capability being changed: *persisting and reading one driver's fingerprint cells
for a (driver, era, vocabulary, channel, measure) slot* — the address it is asked for becomes a
validated value rather than four unchecked strings. No stored value, no fit, and no coverage
number changes.

## Corrections to the issue text (load-bearing)

The issue is right that a defect exists in all three places, but three of its specifics are wrong
and the plan is built on the corrected reading:

1. **H1's premise is false.** "the `CellAddress` value object the fit layer already uses" — the
   fit layer does **not** use `CellAddress`. It appears only inside `store.py` (import + one
   internal construction) and its own unit test; `fit.py` passes the same loose primitives the
   issue objects to.
2. **H1's acceptance is unbuildable as literally written.** "store API typed on `CellAddress`"
   cannot be done: a `CellAddress` names **one cell** (it carries `class_id`), while every store
   method names a whole **k-class slot** and loops over `vocabulary.class_ids` internally. The
   buildable form is a new `FingerprintSlot` value object (= `CellAddress` minus `class_id`),
   with `CellAddress` retained as its per-cell derivation.
3. **H3's assumption is false.** The artifacts are *not* "already ignored via `.agent-work/`" —
   there is no blanket `.agent-work/` rule in `.gitignore`; only `*.pkl` / `*.npz` / `*.db` /
   `scratch/` / `ckpt/` / `backtests/` and a few named record dirs. The archived twins are in
   fact **tracked in git**. H3 therefore widens from a no-op confirmation to a real rule.

## Affected capabilities

- Fingerprint cell persistence and read-back (`struct:physics.fingerprint`, `store.py`) — the
  only capability whose *interface* changes. Its four structural guarantees (non-NULL
  `cell_key`, k-cells-always-populated, loud refusal / no silent substitution, no fit-on-read)
  must survive byte-for-byte in behaviour.
- Stage-G fingerprint fitting (`struct:physics.fingerprint`, `fit.py`) — call-site only; its
  public signature is deliberately unchanged (see decision pressure below).
- End-to-end pilot orchestration (`struct:physics.pilot`) — call-site only, two `get_fingerprint`
  reads.
- Local diagnostic/reproduction runs of the #675 coverage script and the artifact hygiene of a
  live work area — no runtime capability, but both are how a future worktree run is reproduced.

## Structural anchors

- `struct:physics.fingerprint` — the component that owns the change (`src/physics/fingerprint/`:
  `address.py`, `store.py`, `fit.py`).
- `struct:physics.pilot` — downstream consumer, two `get_fingerprint` call sites.
- `struct:physics.instrument_panel` — **adjacent but not a consumer**: it imports only
  `FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS` from `address.py`, never the store. Verified, so it stays out of scope.
- `struct:physics.layer2.pooling` — reused by `fit.py`, untouched here; named so the gate does
  not drift into it.
- `struct:physics` / `struct:utils` — region boundary and the `simplification_limits` checker
  the project requires on touched Python paths.

## Relevant examples / edge cases

- A caller passes `era=""` or `driver=None`: today it reaches a parameterised `SELECT`/`INSERT`
  and returns or writes nothing loudly wrong. After the change it raises at slot construction.
- A caller passes a value containing the `|` `CELL_KEY_DELIMITER`: today two distinct addresses
  could collide into one `cell_key`; the value object already refuses this for cells and must
  refuse it for slots.
- A caller passes an unknown `what_measure`: today `store.write_fingerprint` refuses only the
  *reserved* Build-2 slots; an outright unknown string is refused only later, inside the per-class
  `CellAddress` construction. The slot moves that refusal to the boundary.
- `era` disagreeing with `vocabulary.rules_era`: must **still** raise `EraVocabularyMismatchError`.
  This is the one place the tightening could quietly delete a documented refusal, and it must not.
- A reserved Build-2 `what_measure` is still *constructible* and refused only on write — that
  asymmetry is deliberate and preserved.

## Architecturally meaningful events

- `EraVocabularyMismatchError` on argument inconsistency and on vocabulary drift — a
  boundary-crossing refusal signal other stages rely on.
- `ReservedWhatMeasureError` on a Build-2 dormant slot write.
- `ValueError` from the address/slot value object — the new, earlier failure signal this issue
  exists to create.

## Governing constraints and assumptions

- `constraint:physics_region_no_evo_import` — nothing in this change may import evo /
  `latent_power` / `compound_prior`. Verified none of the touched files does today.
- One canonical path, no compatibility shims or dual-format boundary acceptance
  (`docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md`; `docs/agents/engine-config.json` `rules_root`). This is why the
  store signature change is **breaking**, with every call site migrated in the same gate, rather
  than an additive overload.
- Evidence requirements (`docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md`): `py -m
  src.utils.simplification_limits` on touched `src/` and `tests/` paths; test-led change with the
  focused physics-region suite green.
- Issue-stated exclusion: **no behaviour change to the fit or the coverage computation**.
- Assumption carried forward from the archived #666 run and re-verified here: `data/driver_fingerprint.db`
  is an own-DB artifact, never an `f1_data*.db`; nothing in this change touches DB content or schema.

## Decision anchors and decision pressure

Existing anchors this change sits next to (read-only, none revised):

- `decision:join-consumer-boundary` — the race sim and the panel read un-aggregated cells
  directly. It is why the store's read surface has more consumers than the join does, and why a
  breaking read signature has to be migrated rather than shimmed.
- `claim:instrument_panel_reads_cells_directly` — the claim that keeps `instrument_panel` out of
  this change's blast radius; re-verified (it imports `FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS` only).
- `claim:pilot-runs-end-to-end-3-circuits` — the pilot's end-to-end claim rides on the two
  `get_fingerprint` call sites being migrated correctly.
- `decision:c1_driver_utilization_design`, `decision:pooled_sigma_shared_systematic_floor` —
  reused by the fingerprint fit; untouched, named so the gate does not drift into them.

New decisions this run makes (all commander-self under the principal's standing written
authorization, since no human was reachable; each is surfaced for overturn on return):

- `slot-value-object-not-celladdress` — the store surface is typed on a new `FingerprintSlot`
  (driver, era, channel, what_measure), not on `CellAddress`, because the store's unit is a
  k-class slot. `CellAddress` stays and is derived from the slot per class.
  `@grade: settled/human · leans g2-implement`
- `tightening-stops-at-the-store` — `fit_driver_fingerprints` keeps its public signature and
  builds the slot internally at the store boundary. `@grade: guess · leans g2-implement · settle: if a second caller ever needs to hand fit an address, re-open as its own issue`
- `breaking-not-overloaded` — one canonical store signature; all call sites migrated in one gate.
  `@grade: settled/inherited · leans g2-implement`
- `ignore-live-artifacts-track-archived` — `.gitignore` gets `.agent-work/*/artifacts/*.json`, a
  single-segment glob that ignores a **live** work area while leaving the two-segment-deep
  **archive** path trackable. `@grade: settled/human · leans g1-implement`
- `h2-widens-by-exactly-one-file` — the `sys.path` guard also goes into
  `scripts/pooling_imbalance_validation_665.py`, the only other epic-#659 fingerprint-family script
  missing it (every other family member has it: `fingerprint_bounded_validation.py:27-29`,
  `join_bounded_validation_667.py:41-43`, `instrument_panel_668_report.py:44-45`,
  `build_class_utilization_observables.py:73-75`). #675 mirrors #665's method verbatim and cites it in
  its own docstring, so a worktree run that trips one trips the other. Unrequested scope on a
  recommend-and-defer issue, so it is capped at ONE file, separately attestable inside its gate, and
  named in the PR body rather than smuggled. The ~26 other repo scripts lacking the guard are a
  separate repo-wide sweep → triage.
  `@grade: guess · leans g1-implement · settle: drop the one extra file if the owner reads it as scope creep — the rest of g1 is unaffected`

Decision pressure the gates may force (not yet decisions): whether `address.py` should factor its
per-field validation into one shared helper rather than two near-copies; whether the residual
"`fit` still takes loose primitives" deserves its own issue.

## Claims / evidence surfaces this run must re-confirm

- The store's four structural guarantees still hold after the retype — proven by the module's
  **own pre-existing tests** passing unchanged, not only by new tests
  (`lesson:consumed-frozen-module-run-guard-tests`).
- `constraint:physics_region_no_evo_import` still holds for every touched file.
- The `.gitignore` rule ignores the live path and does **not** shadow the tracked archive path —
  proven by running `git check-ignore` on both, which this planning session could not execute
  (command-permission policy) and which is therefore carried as a gate acceptance check rather
  than an already-closed fact.
- The `sys.path` guard is inserted **before** the first `src.` import — an ordering property, not
  a presence property; a guard placed after the imports is inert.

## Map confidence, staleness, disputes

- `struct:physics.fingerprint` is `status: current`, `confidence: high`, reconciled 2026-07-27 for
  the #659 closeout. The packet's file-level description matches the source read (`fit.py`,
  `store.py`, `address.py`/`vocabulary.py`, `frozen_constants.py`, `join.py`). **No staleness
  found; no scout gate needed.**
- One map-vs-issue dispute, resolved in the map's favour: the map correctly describes `CellAddress`
  as belonging to `address.py`/`vocabulary.py` and never claims the fit layer uses it — the error
  is the issue's, not the map's.
- Nothing in this change alters the map's node set, edges, or purposes; the reconcile step should
  expect a small in-place packet amendment (the `address.py` line gains `FingerprintSlot`), not a
  new node.

## Out of scope

- Any behaviour change to the fit or the coverage computation (issue-stated).
- `fit_driver_fingerprints`' public signature (see `tightening-stops-at-the-store`).
- Collapsing the `era` argument into `vocabulary.rules_era` — that would delete the
  `EraVocabularyMismatchError` argument-consistency refusal, a behaviour change.
- Work areas that write JSON **outside** an `artifacts/` directory, and nested work-id paths two
  segments deep (e.g. `.agent-work/epic-659/665/pooling_verdict.json`) — the chosen single-segment
  glob deliberately does not cover them. Named here rather than silently widened; a triage
  candidate.
- `src/physics/instrument_panel/`, `src/physics/layer2/`, `join.py`, and every evo-region package.
- Committing, pushing, or opening a PR — this engagement is planning-only.
